talks.tip: Use the past simple: went, ate, saw, watched.
questions: What did you do last Saturday, from morning to night?
What was the best moment of the weekend, and why?
What did you eat, and who cooked it?
Who did you see or talk to?
Did anything funny or surprising happen?
What didn't you have time to do?

talks.tip: Use the past simple and used to: I used to play…
questions: Where did you live when you were ten?
What games did you use to play with your friends?
Who was your favourite teacher, and what did they teach?
What did you use to be afraid of?
What was your favourite food when you were small?
Tell me about a birthday you remember.

talks.tip: Use going to for plans: I'm going to visit…
questions: What are you going to do next weekend?
Who are you going to see, and where?
What is one thing you are not going to do?
Where are you going to eat?
What are you going to wear?
What are you going to do if it rains?

talks.tip: Use the present perfect: I have been… I have never…
questions: Have you ever been on a plane? Tell the story.
What is the best film you have ever seen?
Have you ever lost something important? What happened?
Have you ever met someone famous?
What is the most delicious food you have ever eaten?
Have you ever been really lost?
starters: The best … I have ever … was …

talks.tip: He, she or it + -s: my mother cooks, my brother works.
questions: What does your mother or father do on a normal day?
Who in your family gets up first, and what does he or she do?
What does your favourite relative like doing?
What does your brother or sister like to eat?
Who in your family watches TV most, and what does he or she watch?
What does your family do together on Sundays?

talks.tip: Talk about other people too: my boss starts, my friend goes…
questions: What time does your day start, and what do you do first?
What does the person next to you at work or class do?
Who helps you most at work or at school, and how?
What does your teacher or boss say when you are late?
Who works the hardest, and what does he or she do?
What time does your day finish?

talks.tip: Use a, an and the: an egg, a bowl of rice, the best market.
questions: What is the best dish your family makes? Describe how to cook it.
Which do you prefer, a market or a supermarket? Why?
What did you eat for breakfast today?
Can you describe a dish from another country?
What do you eat when you are sick?
What is the strangest food you have ever tried?
starters: An easy dish to cook is …

talks.tip: Use the with superlatives: the busiest, the most beautiful.
questions: Which is better for living, Phnom Penh or the countryside? Why?
What is the most beautiful place you know in Cambodia?
What would you change about our neighbourhood?
What is the busiest place in our city?
Where is the best place to watch the sunset?
What is the most difficult thing about living here?
starters: In the countryside there is a …

talks.tip: Say the -s on plurals clearly: two shirts, three cups, many books.
questions: What things did you buy last month?
How many things are in your bag right now? Name them all.
Do you like shopping online? Why or why not?
What things do you never buy online?
Which shops do you go to most often?
What three things do you need to buy this week?
starters: There are many … in my bag.

talks.tip: Plurals: chairs, windows, plants, and people (no -s).
questions: Describe our home room by room.
How many people and things are in the living room right now?
What three things would you like to change at home?
How many windows and doors are there in our home?
Which rooms do you like best, and why?
What things do we have too many of?

talks.tip: Use 's for owners: my sister's phone, my father's car.
questions: Describe a family member's favourite thing.
Which is better, your phone or your friend's phone? Why?
Tell me about your grandparents' house.
What is your best friend's favourite food?
Whose clothes are the nicest in your family?
Describe your parents' wedding photo or another old photo.

talks.tip: Use at for times, on for days, in for months: at 7, on Monday, in April.
questions: What time do you usually go to bed, and get up?
What do you do on Sundays?
Which month do you like most, and why?
What do you do in the evening after dinner?
What did you do on your last birthday?
What do people in Cambodia do in April?

talks.tip: Mix the past and the present: last year we went…, every year we go…
questions: How did your family celebrate the last Khmer New Year?
What do you do every year at Pchum Ben?
Which holiday do you like most, and why?
What food do you always eat at Khmer New Year?
What did you do last Pchum Ben?
Which holiday would you like to celebrate in another country?

talks.tip: Tell it in order with the past simple: first we met, then we…
questions: Where did we first meet? Tell the story in English.
What was our best day together, and what did we do?
What should we do on our next free day?
What did you think when you first saw me?
What was the funniest thing that happened to us?
Where did we go on our first trip together?

talks.tip: He, she or it + -s: my sister uses, this app shows…
questions: Which app does your family use most, and what does it do?
How has your phone changed your day?
What did people do before smartphones?
What does your mother do on her phone?
Which app helps you most in your day?
What do you do when your phone battery is low?
starters: My mother uses her phone to …
When the battery is low, I …

talks.tip: Watch the small words: good at, interested in, listen to.
questions: Why are you learning English?
What are you good at in English, and what is hard?
What new English word did you learn this week? Use it in a sentence.
What are you interested in reading or watching in English?
Who do you practise English with?
What are you afraid of when you speak English?
